get.description:
Returns one row per tracked keyword for the window between `startDate` and `endDate`. A row is a keyword tracked for one locale and one device — the same text on desktop and mobile is two rows — and it carries the newest rank found in the window on each of the three search engines, the rank at the start of the window, and the difference between them.

Ranks are 1-based positions in the organic results, so a smaller number is better and `googlePositionIncrease` is positive when the keyword moved up. The position fields are `null` when that engine recorded nothing for the keyword inside the window, which is normal for a keyword that was just added: checks are queued and run in the background, so give a new keyword a few days before reading a rank. Only published keywords and those still waiting to be published are listed; unpublished, deleted and archived ones are not.

`page` is 1-based and defaults to 1, `limit` defaults to 50 and is silently reduced to 100 above that, and `pageSize` is the number of pages the result set divides into rather than the number of rows in `items`. Published keywords come before waiting ones whatever `orderBy` says.

The ids `group` accepts come from `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}/group`, and keywords are assigned to groups with `PATCH /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword-group`. For the same window reduced to one figure per engine use `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}/score`; to add keywords use `POST /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword`. `{projectId}` is the numeric project id returned by `GET /v1/project`.

A project that has no Visibility domain record yet, or whose domain has no entry in the ranking store, is answered with 500 and `Domain … not found` or `Host … not found` rather than an empty page.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: First day of the window, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Required: ranks are always reported relative to a window, so there is no default and the earliest recorded check is used as the baseline.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Last day of the window, inclusive, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Required. The newest check on or before this day is the one the position fields report.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Sort key. `keyword` sorts alphabetically by keyword text; `google`, `bing` and `yahoo` sort by the newest rank on that engine; `volume` and `avg_cpc` sort by the research figures for the keyword; `google_increase`, `bing_increase` and `yahoo_increase` sort by places gained on that engine during the window. Keywords with no value for the chosen key sort before ranked ones when `orderDir` is `asc` and after them when it is `desc`. Defaults to `keyword`.

parameters.name: orderDir
parameters.description: Direction of `orderBy`: `asc` for smallest first, `desc` for largest first. Defaults to `asc`. A `desc` direction is the useful one for rank and increase keys, because rank 1 is the best position.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Only return keywords whose text contains this substring, matched anywhere inside the stored text rather than at the start. Trimmed before matching, and omitted or empty means no text filter.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Only return keywords assigned to this group id, from `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}/group`. A negative value such as `-1` returns the keywords in no group at all, and `0` applies no group filter. Omitted means keywords from every group, including none.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Only return keywords tracked for this device: `desktop` for desktop search results, `tablet` or `mobile` for the respective mobile results. Omitted means all three.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Only return keywords tracked in this locale, one of the values from `GET /v1/visibility/locales` such as `en-us`. Omitted means every locale.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page to return, 1-based, so the first page is `1` and not `0`. Defaults to 1. A page past the end returns an empty `items` array with the real `total` intact.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 50; any value above 100 is reduced to 100 rather than rejected, and `limit` in the response repeats the value actually used.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project id: the value returned by the create endpoints, and the `id` of each row from `GET /v1/project`.

total.description: Number of keywords matching the filters, across every page — not the number of rows in `items`.

limit.description: Page size applied to this response: the requested `limit`, capped at 100.

pageSize.description: Number of pages the result set divides into at the applied `limit`. This is a page count, not the number of rows returned, and it is 0 when nothing matched.

bingPositionIncrease.description: Places gained on Bing during the window: the starting rank minus the newest rank. Positive is an improvement, negative a drop. `null` when either end is missing.

yahooPosition.description: Newest Yahoo rank in the window: a 1-based organic position, where 1 is the top result. `null` when Yahoo did not record the keyword inside the window.

yahooPositionStart.description: Yahoo rank at the start of the window, 1-based. `null` when Yahoo recorded nothing in the window.

yahooPositionIncrease.description: Places gained on Yahoo during the window: the starting rank minus the newest rank. Positive is an improvement, negative a drop. `null` when either end is missing.

get.description:
Summarizes the project’s tracked keywords over `startDate` to `endDate` as one block of numbers per search engine, for a scorecard or a trend line rather than a table of keywords.

Field names inside a block follow two conventions. A trailing `0` is the value at the **start** of the window — the earliest rank recorded for each keyword — so `visibilityScore0` is what visibility was before the period began. `Inc` is the change over the window, current minus start, so a positive `…Inc` always means movement in the good direction: a higher visibility percentage, a better average position, more keywords in a rank bucket. `r1tor3`, `r4tor10`, `r11tor50` and `r51tor100` are rank buckets, counting keywords whose newest position falls in that range.

Only keywords that are actively tracked are counted; those still waiting for the account’s keyword allowance are ignored, exactly as `enabled` marks them in `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}`. The ranks are read for the project’s own domain across every locale, device and group it has keywords for — unlike the keyword list, the call has no filter parameters. Each engine is computed independently over the same keyword set, so Bing and Yahoo can be all zeros while Google has figures.

A project whose keywords have never been checked returns zeros rather than nulls: `visibilityScore` falls back to 0 when no keyword has a search volume, and the counts are 0. For the individual rows behind these numbers use `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}` with the same two dates, and for one keyword’s history use `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}/{keywordId}`. `{projectId}` is the numeric project id returned by `GET /v1/project`.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: First day of the window, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Required, with no default: every `…0` field and every `…Inc` field is measured from the earliest check on or after this day.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Last day of the window, inclusive, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Required. The newest check on or before this day is the one the non-`0` fields report.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project id: the value returned by the create endpoints, and the `id` of each row from `GET /v1/project`.

200.description: One block per search engine. A trailing `0` on a field name is the value at the start of the window; `Inc` is the change over the window, current minus start, so a positive `…Inc` is an improvement. `r1tor3`, `r4tor10`, `r11tor50` and `r51tor100` are rank buckets. Every field is present and numeric, 0 rather than null when there was nothing to measure.

google.description: Score block for Google. `null` only when a block could not be produced; the handler always produces one, zeroed when nothing has been checked.

visibilityScore.description: Volume-weighted visibility on this engine at the end of the window, as a percentage of the best possible score: `visibilityRawScore` divided by `volumeTotal`, times 100. 100 would mean every tracked keyword ranks first; 0 when no keyword has a search volume.

visibilityScore0.description: The same visibility percentage computed from the ranks at the start of the window — the figure `visibilityScoreInc` is measured from.

visibilityScoreInc.description: Change in the visibility percentage over the window, `visibilityScore` minus `visibilityScore0`. Positive means visibility improved.

visibilityRawScore.description: Unnormalised visibility: for each keyword, `(100 - (rank - 1)) / 100` multiplied by its search volume, summed. A keyword ranked first contributes its whole volume, one ranked 100th contributes almost nothing. A top-ten keyword with no recorded volume is counted as volume 1.

visibilityRawScore0.description: The same sum computed from the ranks at the start of the window.

visibilityTotal.description: Number of keywords behind `visibilityScore`: those with a rank and a volume at the end of the window, where a top-ten keyword with no recorded volume counts as volume 1. A keyword with neither adds nothing to visibility and is not counted.

volumeTotal.description: Combined search volume of the keywords recorded at either end of the window, each one added once. It is the denominator of the visibility percentage, so it also holds the volume of keywords that have a starting rank but no newest one, which pulls the score down; 0 when nothing was recorded.

incPosition.description: Number of keywords that improved during the window — their rank number got smaller. The same event that makes `googlePositionIncrease` positive on a row of `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}`.

decPosition.description: Number of keywords that dropped during the window — their rank number got larger.

totalPosition.description: Sum of the newest ranks of every keyword that had one. Divide by `totalPositionCount` to get `avgPosition`.

totalPosition0.description: Sum of the starting ranks of every keyword that had one.

totalPositionCount.description: Number of keywords that had a rank at the end of the window. 0 when none has been checked yet.

totalPositionCount0.description: Number of keywords that had a rank at the start of the window.

avgPosition.description: Mean newest rank, rounded to two decimals; 0 when `totalPositionCount` is 0. Lower is better.

avgPosition0.description: Mean rank at the start of the window, rounded to two decimals; 0 when there were no ranks.

avgPositionInc.description: Improvement in the mean rank, `avgPosition0` minus `avgPosition`. Positive means the average position got better, even though the number itself went down.

r1tor3position.description: Number of keywords whose newest rank is 1 to 3 — the top of the first page at the end of the window.

r1tor3position0.description: Number of keywords ranked 1 to 3 at the start of the window.

r4tor10position.description: Number of keywords whose newest rank is 4 to 10 — the rest of the first page.

totalPosition0.description: Sum of the starting ranks of every keyword that had one.

totalPositionCount.description: Number of keywords that had a rank at the end of the window. 0 when none has been checked yet.

totalPositionCount0.description: Number of keywords that had a rank at the start of the window.

avgPosition.description: Mean newest rank, rounded to two decimals; 0 when `totalPositionCount` is 0. Lower is better.

avgPosition0.description: Mean rank at the start of the window, rounded to two decimals; 0 when there were no ranks.

r1tor3position0.description: Number of keywords ranked 1 to 3 at the start of the window.

r4tor10position.description: Number of keywords whose newest rank is 4 to 10 — the rest of the first page.

r11tor50position.description: Number of keywords whose newest rank is 11 to 50 — pages two to five.

r51tor100position.description: Number of keywords whose newest rank is 51 to 100 — pages six to ten. A rank past 100 falls into none of the four buckets.

get.description:
Returns the keyword groups defined for the project, each with the id that `PATCH /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword-group` assigns keywords to and that the `group` filter on `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}` accepts. A live group is listed whether or not keywords currently point at it.

Groups are how a project’s keywords are split into topics so a report can be read one topic at a time. This is the first step of the chain: create a group with `POST /v1/visibility/{projectId}/group`, add keywords with `POST /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword`, then file them with `PATCH /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword-group`.

A group deleted with `DELETE /v1/visibility/{projectId}/group/{groupId}` disappears from this list, but its keywords keep the assignment: they still report the old group name in `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}` and are still returned when filtering by that id. `{projectId}` is the numeric project id returned by `GET /v1/project`.

name.description: Name the group was created with, unique within the project and shown against each of its keywords.

groups.description: Groups that are live for this project. Deleted groups are not returned, even while keywords still point at them.

post.description:
Creates a group for splitting the project’s keywords into topics, and returns it with its `id`. That id is what `PATCH /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword-group` takes as `groupId`, what `POST /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword` takes as `group`, and what the `group` filter of `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}` accepts.

Names are unique within a project and this call is safe to repeat: asking for a name that already exists does not fail and does not add a second group — the existing one comes back with its own id, and a group deleted earlier is revived under its old id rather than recreated. Keywords keep their group across a revive, because deleting a group never unassigned them.

A group is not a precondition for tracking keywords: `POST /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword` accepts keywords with no group, and they can be filed later. `{projectId}` is the numeric project id returned by `GET /v1/project`.

id.description: ID of the group, whether it was just created, already existed, or was revived after deletion.

name.description: Name of the group as it was stored, trimmed of surrounding whitespace.

delete.description:
Takes a group out of service: it stops appearing in `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}/group` and so from any list a client builds from it.

The keywords filed under it are **not** unassigned. They keep their assignment, still report the deleted group’s name in `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}`, and are still returned by `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}?group={groupId}` — no ranking history is touched either. To move them somewhere else, send them to another group, or to `null` for no group at all, with `PATCH /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword-group`. Recreating a group with the same name later revives this one under the same id, which brings its keywords back into view with it.

The group has to exist and still be live, but a missing one is not a 404: an id that does not exist, belongs to another project, or was already deleted is answered with 500. `{projectId}` is the numeric project id returned by `GET /v1/project`.

parameters.description: Numeric id of the project the group belongs to, as returned by `GET /v1/project`.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description: ID of the group to delete, from `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}/group` or `POST /v1/visibility/{projectId}/group`.

200.description: The group is no longer live.

id.description: ID of the group that was taken out of service, echoed back so the caller can confirm which one it deleted.

post.description:
Adds up to 100 keywords to the project in one call and returns their ids, one per entry of `keywords`, in the order sent. A keyword is identified by its text together with `locale` and `device`, so sending a combination that already exists returns the existing id instead of creating a duplicate — the call is safe to repeat, and repeating it with a different `group` does not move the keywords either.

Tracking is queued, not immediate. New keywords are only queued for checking while the account still has room under its keyword allowance; an account at its limit has the keywords stored but left inactive, and they appear in `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}` with `enabled` of `false` and no positions until room frees up. Checks then run in the background over the following days, and no endpoint reports progress per keyword — poll `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}` and read the position fields, which stay `null` until the first check lands.

The returned ids are what `PATCH /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword-group` files into a group and what `PATCH /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword-setting` moves to another locale or device. Group ids come from `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}/group`, and locales from `GET /v1/visibility/locales`. `{projectId}` is the numeric project id returned by `GET /v1/project`. A project with no Visibility domain record is answered with 500, and nothing is added.

locale.description: Locale whose search results the keywords are tracked in, one of the values from `GET /v1/visibility/locales`. Defaults to `en-us`. Rankings are per locale, so the same keyword in two locales is two tracked keywords with separate history.

device.description: Device whose search results the keywords are tracked on: `desktop`, `tablet` or `mobile`. Defaults to `desktop`. Each device is tracked separately, so tracking desktop and mobile takes two entries in the result.

group.description: ID of an existing group, from `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}/group`, to file the new keywords under. Omitted means no group. The group must belong to the same account, and an id from another account fails with 500 rather than being ignored.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Numeric id of the project the keywords are added to, as returned by `GET /v1/project`.

200.description: The ids of the keywords, whether they were created now or already existed.

ids.description: IDs of the tracked keywords, one per entry of `keywords` and in the same order, so the first id belongs to the first keyword sent. These are the `id` values of `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}` and the ids the two `PATCH` endpoints expect.

patch.description:
Files each keyword under a group, replacing whichever group it was in. This is the third step of the usual chain: create the group with `POST /v1/visibility/{projectId}/group`, add the keywords with `POST /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword`, then pass both sets of ids here.

IDs that do not belong to this project are dropped without an error, so compare the `ids` in the response with the ones sent: it lists only what was actually reassigned, and an empty array means nothing matched. Passing `null` as `groupId` is how a keyword is returned to no group, which is the set `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}?group=-1` lists.

Assignment is the only thing the call changes. Ranks, history and the keyword’s locale and device are untouched — for those use `PATCH /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword-setting`. `{projectId}` is the numeric project id returned by `GET /v1/project`.

groupId.description: ID of the group to assign, from `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}/group`, or `null` to take the keywords out of any group. Defaults to `null`. A group that does not exist or belongs to another project fails the whole request with 500.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project id: the value returned by the create endpoints, and the `id` of each row from `GET /v1/project`.

200.description: The keywords that now carry the requested group.

ids.description: IDs of the keywords that were actually reassigned. Shorter than the request when some ids belong to another project, and an empty array when none matched.

patch.description:
Moves keywords to a different locale or device — the pair that decides which search results their rank is read from. Use it when a keyword was added in the wrong market, or when the same keyword should also be tracked from another country. It is the counterpart of `PATCH /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword-group`, which changes only the grouping.

Each keyword succeeds or fails on its own, so read `result` rather than the status code: a 200 does not mean every keyword moved. A keyword that already has ranking history is refused, because the positions recorded so far were measured for the old locale and device and would not describe the new pairing; so is a keyword that would collide with one already tracked for the same text under the target locale and device. In practice only keywords that have not been checked yet can be moved, so to track an active keyword in another market, add it again with `POST /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword` under the new locale and device and let it build its own history.

IDs from another project are filtered out before the work starts and do not appear in `result` at all, so the array can be shorter than `ids`. Locale values come from `GET /v1/visibility/locales`. `{projectId}` is the numeric project id returned by `GET /v1/project`.

ids.description: IDs of the keywords to change, at least one, as returned by `POST /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword` or read from `id` in `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}`. IDs belonging to another project are ignored and are not reported back in `result`.

locale.description: Locale to move the keywords to, one of the values from `GET /v1/visibility/locales`. Required, with no default here — unlike `POST /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword` there is no `en-us` fallback, so the target market always has to be stated.

device.description: Device to move the keywords to: `desktop`, `tablet` or `mobile`. Required, with no default here. Together with `locale` it is what identifies the keyword, so moving to a pair already used by the same text is refused for that keyword.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Numeric id of the project the keywords belong to, as returned by `GET /v1/project`.

200.description: Per-keyword outcome of the move.

id.description: ID of the keyword this entry reports on, as sent in `ids`. Keywords from another project have no entry.

updated.description: `true` when the locale and device were written for this keyword, `false` when it was skipped. The response status is 200 either way, so a partial failure is only visible here.

error.description: Why the keyword was skipped: `Cannot update keyword with existing stats` when it already has ranking history, `Keyword already exists with different locale and device` when another keyword of the project already occupies the target pair, or the database error code for any other failure. `null` when `updated` is `true`.

result.description: One entry per keyword that was considered, each reporting success or the reason it was left alone. The order is not guaranteed to match `ids`.

get.description:
Returns one keyword with its day-by-day rank on one search engine, for drawing a trend line or finding the day a position changed. Each entry of `data` is a day on which the engine recorded the keyword, ordered oldest first, so the gaps between dates are days that were not checked — not days at position 0.

`{keywordId}` is the `id` of a row from `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}`, not the internal keyword id. The keyword’s own locale and device decide which search results were read, and `service` picks the engine, so a chart covering three engines takes three calls with the same dates. The id is not checked against this project, so an id from another project is accepted and normally comes back with an empty `data` array.

For the same window reduced to one figure per engine use `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}/score`, and for the row this keyword occupies in the project use `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}`. `{projectId}` is the numeric project id returned by `GET /v1/project`. An id that does not exist is not answered with 404: the lookup fails before the reply and the request ends as 500.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: First day of the history, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Required; days before it are never returned even when they were checked.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Last day of the history, inclusive, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Required.

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Search engine whose positions are returned: `google`, `bing` or `yahoo`. Defaults to `google`. One call reports one engine, so each additional engine costs another call over the same dates.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project id: the value returned by the create endpoints, and the `id` of each row from `GET /v1/project`.

parameters.name: keywordId
parameters.description: ID of a keyword, as returned by `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}`.

200.description: The keyword and its daily positions on one engine.

id.description: ID of the tracked keyword, the same value that was requested.

keyword.description: Keyword text, lower-cased as the application stores it.

locale.description: Locale the keyword is tracked in. The returned positions were read from that locale’s search results, not from every locale the keyword appears in.

device.description: Device the positions were measured on: `desktop`, `tablet` or `mobile`.

date.description: Day the rank was recorded, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Entries are ordered by this value, oldest first.

position.description: Rank on that day on the requested engine: a 1-based organic position, where 1 is the top result and a larger number is worse.

link.description: URL that was ranked for the keyword on that day, as the ranking store recorded it.

data.description: One entry per checked day inside the window, oldest first. Empty when the keyword was not checked on any day in the window, which is also the answer for a keyword that has only just been added.

post.description:
Starts an accessibility check of a project and returns the id of the run it queued. The work is asynchronous: the response carries an id, not results, and the checker starts on its own. It answers `200`, not `201`, even though it creates a run, so match on the body rather than on the status code.

Watch the run with `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}`, where the page count, the problem counts and `score` appear as it progresses, and per page with `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}`, where each page moves from `pending` to `running` to `finished`. `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/score` then reports the finished run’s score.

If the project has a stored login recipe, the run reuses it and may pause on a prompt such as a one-time code; `loginInputs` lists those prompts in the order the checker walks them. Once `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}/login-inputs` reports one as ready, answer it with `PUT /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}/login-inputs/{inputId}`. For any other project `loginInputs` is empty and the run needs no answers.

`guidelines` defaults to `["WCAG22-AAA"]`, and `reportSettings` defaults to recording likely and potential problems with manual checks off.

guidelines.description: Guideline sets to check the pages against, one entry per standard and level. `WCAG2-A`, `WCAG2-AA` and `WCAG2-AAA` are WCAG 2.0 at levels A, AA and AAA; `WCAG21-*` is WCAG 2.1 and `WCAG22-*` is WCAG 2.2 at the same three levels; `WCAG1-*` is WCAG 1.0. `BITV1` is the German BITV 1.0 catalogue, `508` the United States Section 508 catalogue, and `STANCA` the Italian Stanca Act catalogue, each of which is a single set rather than a level. Defaults to `["WCAG22-AAA"]`.

likelyProblems.description: Record likely problems: findings the checker believes are violations but cannot confirm without a person inspecting the page. Defaults to `true` when `reportSettings`, or this key, is omitted.

potentialProblems.description: Record potential problems: findings that may be violations depending on runtime or human judgement. Defaults to `true` when omitted.

manualTests.description: Include the manual checks, which the automated run cannot decide and a person has to complete in the application. Only takes effect when `likelyProblems` or `potentialProblems` is also enabled — otherwise it is stored as `false`. Defaults to `false`.

reportSettings.description: Which classes of problem the run records. Omit it to record likely and potential problems and no manual checks.

inputs.description: Values for the prompts of the project’s login recipe, in the order the recipe asks for them — usually the username followed by the password. Encrypted per project before storage, and never returned by any endpoint.

basicAuth.description: HTTP basic-auth credentials, when the site is protected by basic authentication instead of a sign-in form.

username.description: Username for HTTP basic authentication, for a site protected at the server rather than by a sign-in form.

password.description: Password for HTTP basic authentication, encrypted per project before storage.

authOptions.description: Credentials for a project that signs in, such as a private SharePoint team site or a project created from a URL with authentication. Only used when the project has a stored login recipe; for any other project the run signs in with nothing and this object has no effect. Omit it for a public project.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project. IDs come from `GET /v1/project`; a project this account cannot read answers `404` before the handler runs, and an id that is not a number answers `500`.

200.description: The id of the queued run and any login prompts it will pause on.

id.description: ID of the run that was queued. It is the `reportId` every other accessibility report endpoint takes, and the run appears in `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}` straight away.
0-based position of the prompt in the run’s stored login recipe. It is the `inputId` the submit endpoint takes, and it stays the same for the whole run.

label.description: Short prompt to show the person answering, for example `Microsoft Authenticator approval`. `Input` when the recipe gave the prompt no label.

description.description: Longer explanation of the value expected for this prompt. An empty string when the recipe gave none, never `null`.

loginInputs.description: Prompts the run may pause on, in the order the checker walks them. Empty when the project does not sign in, or when its login recipe asks for nothing deferred. Answer them with `PUT /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}/login-inputs/{inputId}`.

get.description:
Lists the accessibility runs of one project, newest first, one row per run. `id` is the run id, and it is the `reportId` that every other accessibility report endpoint takes — the page list, the problems and groups summaries, the per-page detail and the login prompts. So this is the call that turns a project id into a report id.

Runs that were deleted are not listed. `limit` and `page` are both 1-based; `limit` defaults to 20 and is lowered to 1000 if you ask for more. A run is created by `POST /v1/accessibility/{projectId}` and is checked asynchronously, so a run that was just queued appears here with `urls`, the problem counts and `score` still `null`, and fills them in as the checker progresses.

A `403` answering `unauthorized_access` means the token’s account cannot read this project; a `403` answering `feature_disabled` means its plan does not include Accessibility.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of runs to return. Defaults to 20. Values above 1000 are lowered to 1000 rather than rejected.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number to return. Defaults to 1, which is the newest run.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project. IDs come from `GET /v1/project`; a project this account cannot read answers `404` before the handler runs, and an id that is not a number answers `500`.

200.description: A page of accessibility runs, newest first.

total.description: Number of runs the project has, ignoring paging, so `ceil(total / limit)` pages are available.

limit.description: Page size that was applied — the `limit` you sent, capped at 1000, or 20 when you sent none.

pageSize.description: Number of pages at this `limit`, `ceil(total / limit)`, not the number of rows in this response.

id.description: ID of the run. This is the `reportId` of `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}` and of every other endpoint that works on one report, and `PUT`/`DELETE` on the same paths take it too.

scheduled.description: Whether this run was created by the scheduled accessibility check rather than started on demand. The flag is read from the run and passed through.

urls.description: Number of pages the run checked. `null` until the run has counted them; a queued run has none yet.

guidelines.description: Guideline sets this run checks, using the codes accepted by `POST /v1/accessibility/{projectId}` — for example `WCAG22-AAA`. Empty when the run recorded none.

error.description: Message the run ended with when it failed. `null` when it has not failed, including while it is still running.

errorReason.description: The checker’s own reason for `error`, in its words rather than a fixed vocabulary. `null` when it recorded none.

knownProblems.description: Known problems across the run’s pages: findings the checker is certain are violations. `null` until the run has produced counts.

likelyProblems.description: Likely problems: findings the checker believes are violations but cannot confirm without a person inspecting the page. `null` until the run has produced counts.

potentialProblems.description: Potential problems: findings that may be violations depending on runtime or human judgement. `null` until the run has produced counts.

groups.description: Number of guideline groups the run evaluated — the WCAG guidelines, such as `1.1 Text Alternatives`, that checks are filed under. `null` until the run has produced counts.

groupsFailed.description: How many of those groups produced at least one problem on at least one page. `null` until the run has produced counts.

groupsPassed.description: How many of those groups had no problem on any page. `null` until the run has produced counts.

score.description: Score stored for the run, rounded to two decimals and left unscaled: multiply it by 100 to read it the way `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/score` reports the latest run. `null` until the run finishes.

created.description: ISO 8601 date and time the run was created.

id.description: 0-based position of the prompt in the run’s stored login recipe. It is the `inputId` the submit endpoint takes, and it stays the same for the whole run.

label.description: Short prompt to show the person answering, for example `Microsoft Authenticator approval`. `Input` when the recipe gave the prompt no label.

description.description: Longer explanation of the value expected for this prompt. An empty string when the recipe gave none, never `null`.

loginInputs.description: Prompts this run may pause on, in the order the checker walks them, so a client can ask before they are needed. Only the user who started the run sees them; empty for anyone else and for projects that do not sign in. Answer one with `PUT /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}/login-inputs/{inputId}`.

items.description: The page of runs, newest first.

get.description:
Returns the login prompts an accessibility run may be waiting on, with the current state of each. Authenticated projects reuse the crawl’s login recipe, so a run can pause for a deferred value such as an MFA code; poll the call until an item reports `ready: 1`, then submit it with `PUT /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}/login-inputs/{inputId}`.

Only the user who started the run sees its prompts: a colleague with access to the same project can read the report but gets an empty `items` array here. The list is also empty for a project that does not sign in. A slot that can no longer be read — it expired about an hour after the run created it — reports `completed: 1` rather than `ready: 1`, so it will never become answerable; start a new run with `POST /v1/accessibility/{projectId}` to get fresh prompts.

`reportId` must be a run of this project that has not been deleted. Anything else answers `404` with `accessibility_report_not_found`, which is also what a report belonging to another account gets.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project the run belongs to.

parameters.name: reportId
parameters.description: ID of the accessibility run — the `id` from `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}`, or the `id` that `POST /v1/accessibility/{projectId}` returned.

200.description: The run’s login prompts and the state of each.

id.description: 0-based position of the prompt in the run’s stored login recipe. It is the `inputId` the submit endpoint takes, and it stays the same for the whole run.

label.description: Short prompt to show the person answering, for example `Microsoft Authenticator approval`. `Input` when the recipe gave the prompt no label.

description.description: Longer explanation of the value expected for this prompt. An empty string when the recipe gave none, never `null`.

ready.description: `1` once the checker has reached this prompt and is waiting for an answer, `0` while it has not got there yet. Only an input at `1` can usefully be answered.

completed.description: `1` once the value has been submitted, or once the slot has expired and can no longer be answered, `0` while it is still waiting. A slot that has expired reports `1` here so a client never polls it forever.

value.description: Value currently held for this prompt: what a previous submit stored, or the text the run itself filled in (the authenticator prompt puts the number to match here). An empty string when nothing has been written, never `null`.

items.description: Every prompt of this run, in the order the checker walks them and including ones that are already answered or expired, so the positions are stable across polls. Empty when the run has no prompts or was started by another user.

put.description:
Answers one prompt of a waiting accessibility run, releasing it to continue signing in. Omit `value` — send an empty object — when the prompt already carries the value the checker needs, such as a Microsoft Authenticator approval where the run reports the number to match and only waits to be told to continue; the input is then marked complete and the value the run filled in is left as it is. A `value` that is sent must not be empty.

`inputId` is the position reported by `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}/login-inputs`, and that call is also how you know a prompt is ready to be answered. Answers `404` with `login_input_not_found` when the position does not exist for this run — including when the run belongs to another user, whose prompts you cannot see — and `login_input_expired` when the slot has timed out, in which case start a new run to request a fresh one.

A successful answer affects this prompt only; other prompts of the run stay pending until answered or expired.

value.description: The value to hand to the checker, such as a one-time code. Omit the key entirely to mark a prompt complete without changing the value the run filled in; an empty string is rejected by validation.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project the run belongs to.

parameters.name: reportId
parameters.description: ID of the accessibility run — the `id` from `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}`.

parameters.name: inputId
parameters.description: 0-based position of the prompt in the run, as returned in `items[].id` by `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}/login-inputs`.

200.description: The prompt that was released.

id.description: 0-based position of the prompt that was answered — the `inputId` you sent.

completed.description: Always `true`. The call either releases the prompt or fails, so there is no `false` case to handle.

delete.description:
Deletes one accessibility run, not all results for the project: the run you name is marked deleted and drops out of `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}`, while the project’s other runs stay and keep feeding `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/score`. A check that is still running for it is canceled first, and the run is marked deleted even if that cancellation call fails, so the delete itself does not report the failure.

Returns the id of the run it deleted. A `reportId` that is not a run of this project, a run that belongs to another account, and a run that is already deleted all answer `500` with an explanatory `message` rather than a `404` — and so does a `reportId` that is not a number. Check the id before deleting rather than handling a missing-run response.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project. IDs come from `GET /v1/project`; a project this account cannot read answers `404` before the handler runs, and an id that is not a number answers `500`.

parameters.name: reportId
parameters.description: ID of the accessibility run — the `id` from `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}`. It is not checked here, so an id that is not a run of this project answers `500` from the handler rather than `404`.

200.description: The id of the run that was deleted.

id.description: ID of the run that was deleted — the `reportId` you sent, which is no longer listed by `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}`.

get.description:
Lists the pages of one accessibility run, one row per checked page, with what the checker found on it. `reportId` is a run id from `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}`; a run that belongs to another project, or an id that is not a run at all, answers `500` rather than `404`.

`id` is the row id and is what `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}/{itemId}` takes; `itemId` is the page’s own id inside the project, so the two are different values. Each row carries its lifecycle in `state` (`pending`, `running`, `finished`), the three problem counts and the page’s score, so one call is enough to show a run while it is still going.

`group` and `subgroup` take the ids from `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}/groups` and keep only pages that have a problem in that group. `search` matches the page URL and is read as a regular expression when it is wrapped in slashes — except together with `group` or `subgroup`, where it is always a plain substring. Paging is `limit`/`page`, both 1-based; `limit` defaults to 50 and is lowered to 100 if you ask for more.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Only return pages with at least one problem in this guideline group. Pass the `id` of a group from `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}/groups`; omit it to include every group.

parameters.name: subgroup
parameters.description: Only return pages with at least one problem in this subgroup. Pass a subgroup `id` from `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}/groups`; combine it with `group` to narrow further.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Field to order by: `known_problems`, `likely_problems` or `potential_problems` order by that count on the page, `created` by when the page row was created, `id` by the row id. Defaults to `id`.

parameters.name: orderDir
parameters.description: Direction applied to `orderBy`, defaulting to `desc`. Ordering by `id` ignores it and is always ascending, so paging stays stable.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Substring matched against the page URL. Wrap it in slashes, such as `/^\/blog\//`, to have it used as a regular expression; with `group` or `subgroup` set it is always a plain substring.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of pages to return. Defaults to 50; values above 100 are lowered to 100 rather than rejected.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number to return. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project the run belongs to. A project this account cannot read answers `404` before the handler runs.

parameters.name: reportId
parameters.description: ID of the accessibility run — the `id` from `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}`, or the `id` that `POST /v1/accessibility/{projectId}` returned. It is not checked here, so an id that is not a run of this project answers `500` from the handler rather than `404`.

200.description: A page of the run’s checked pages.

total.description: Number of pages in the run matching the filters, ignoring paging — `ceil(total / limit)` pages are available.

limit.description: Page size that was applied: the `limit` you sent capped at 100, or 50 when you sent none.

pageSize.description: Number of pages at this `limit`, `ceil(total / limit)`, not the number of rows in this response.

id.description: ID of this page’s result row. This is the `itemId` in the path of `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}/{itemId}`.

itemId.description: ID the checker recorded for the crawled page itself, inside the project. It is not the id the detail endpoint takes — use `id` for that — and two runs report the same `itemId` for the same page.

url.description: URL of the page that was checked. An empty string when the run did not record one.

state.description: Lifecycle of this page’s check: `pending` while it is queued, `running` while the checker is on it, `finished` once it has results. `unknown` for any stored value the API does not recognize.

status.description: Status text the checker stores beside `state`, passed through as recorded. It is prose rather than a fixed set, so read `state` for the lifecycle.

knownProblems.description: Known problems on this page: findings the checker is certain are violations. `0` when there are none or the page has not been checked yet.

likelyProblems.description: Likely problems on this page: findings the checker believes are violations but cannot confirm without a person looking. `0` when there are none.

potentialProblems.description: Potential problems on this page: findings that may be violations depending on runtime or human judgement. `0` when there are none.

archivedKnownProblems.description: Known problems on this page that have since been archived, so they are kept for history but no longer counted in `knownProblems`. `0` when nothing is archived.

archivedLikelyProblems.description: Likely problems on this page that have since been archived and are no longer counted in `likelyProblems`. `0` when nothing is archived.

archivedPotentialProblems.description: Potential problems on this page that have since been archived and are no longer counted in `potentialProblems`. `0` when nothing is archived.

groupsChecked.description: Number of guideline groups the checker evaluated on this page — the WCAG guidelines, such as `1.1 Text Alternatives`. `0` before the page has been checked.

groupsFailed.description: How many of those groups produced at least one problem on this page.

groupsPassed.description: How many of those groups produced no problem on this page.

score.description: Score the checker recorded for this page, unscaled — unlike `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/score` it is not multiplied by 100. `0` when no score was recorded.

processError.description: Error the checker hit while processing this page. `null` when it processed the page without one.

created.description: ISO 8601 date and time the page row was created.

items.description: The page of results. Empty when no page of the run matches the filters.

get.description:
Returns the finished accessibility runs of a project as a time series, oldest first, for charting how a project’s accessibility has moved: one row per run with its id, when it ran, its three problem counts and its score. Only runs that finished, checked at least one page and recorded no error are included, so failed attempts do not interrupt the series.

With neither date it returns the 100 most recent qualifying runs, still in ascending order. With `startDate` and/or `endDate` it returns every qualifying run in the range. This is the data that `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/score` reduces to a single number, and the run ids are accepted by `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}`.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Earliest creation date to include, as `YYYY-MM-DD`; runs created that day are included. Omit to start from the project’s first qualifying run.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Latest creation date to include, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, compared at midnight of that day — so a run later on the same day falls outside the range and you should pass the following day to include it. Omit to run up to the newest qualifying run.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project. IDs come from `GET /v1/project`; a project this account cannot read answers `404` before the handler runs, and an id that is not a number answers `500`.

200.description: A project’s finished runs, oldest first.

id.description: ID of the run — the `reportId` the other accessibility endpoints take.

date.description: ISO 8601 date and time the run was created. The series is ordered by this, ascending.

knownProblems.description: Known problems the run recorded — findings the checker is certain are violations.

likelyProblems.description: Likely problems the run recorded — findings it believes are violations but cannot confirm without a person looking.

potentialProblems.description: Potential problems the run recorded — findings that may be violations depending on runtime or human judgement.

score.description: Score the run recorded, `0` when it recorded none. It is stored unscaled: multiply by 100 to compare it with `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/score`.

data.description: Qualifying runs in ascending date order. Empty when the project has no finished run in the range.

get.description:
Returns one number for the project’s current accessibility plus the per-page averages behind it, read from the two most recent runs that have results — finished runs, plus a run that is still pending but has already recorded pages. `score` is the latest of those runs’ stored score multiplied by 100, while the same run’s score appears unscaled in `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}`, so this is the value to show on a dashboard.

The two runs are also compared: the `moved*` fields give the change since the previous run, which is what an “improving or worsening” indicator needs. Every field is `0` when the project has no run with results, so a project that was never checked reads exactly like one that scored zero — check that a run exists before treating `0` as a result.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project. IDs come from `GET /v1/project`; a project this account cannot read answers `404` before the handler runs, and an id that is not a number answers `500`.

200.description: The project’s current score and the averages behind it.

score.description: Current score, the latest run with results multiplied by 100, so a 0–100 value. `0` when the project has no run with results.

avgKnownProblems.description: Known problems per page in the latest run: total known problems divided by pages checked, rounded up. `0` when the project has no run with results.

avgLikelyProblems.description: Likely problems per page in the latest run, total divided by pages checked and rounded up. `0` when there is no run with results.

avgPotentialProblems.description: Potential problems per page in the latest run, total divided by pages checked and rounded up. `0` when there is no run with results.

movedAvgKnownProblems.description: Change in `avgKnownProblems` since the previous run, as a percentage of the smaller of the two averages; positive means more problems. `0` when there is no previous run or either average is `0`, because the ratio is undefined.

movedAvgLikelyProblems.description: Change in `avgLikelyProblems` since the previous run, as a percentage of the smaller of the two averages; positive means more problems. `0` when there is no previous run or either average is `0`.

movedAvgPotentialProblems.description: Change in `avgPotentialProblems` since the previous run, as a percentage of the smaller of the two averages; positive means more problems. `0` when there is no previous run or either average is `0`.

get.description:
Summarizes one run by guideline group: one row per group with how many problems it produced and how many pages it touched. Rows are keyed by the group name trimmed to its numbered prefix, so the subgroups under one guideline — the WCAG guidelines `1.1` to `4.1` — are summed into a single row. Use `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}/groups` when the subgroup breakdown is needed instead.

Counts are relative to the run’s own page total, which is reported as `totalPages` and includes pages that had no problem at all. Only groups that produced at least one problem appear, so a run that found nothing answers an empty array. A run of another project, or an id that is not a run, answers `500` rather than `404`.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project the run belongs to. A project this account cannot read answers `404` before the handler runs.

parameters.name: reportId
parameters.description: ID of the accessibility run — the `id` from `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}`, or the `id` that `POST /v1/accessibility/{projectId}` returned. It is not checked here, so an id that is not a run of this project answers `500` from the handler rather than `404`.

200.description: The run’s problems summed per guideline group.

title.description: Name of the guideline group, trimmed to its numbered prefix — for example `1.1 Text Alternatives` with any subgroup detail after a colon removed.

totalPages.description: Number of pages the run checked, used as the denominator for `pagesPassed`. `0` when the run recorded no page count.

problems.description: Number of problem instances this group recorded across all pages, counting every occurrence rather than every page.

pagesWithProblems.description: Number of pages with at least one problem in this group. Never more than `totalPages`.

pagesPassed.description: Number of pages with no problem in this group: `totalPages` minus `pagesWithProblems`, never negative.

problems.description: One row per group that produced a problem, sorted by group name. Empty when the run found nothing.

get.description:
Returns the guideline groups and subgroups that a run found problems in, as a tree: a group is a WCAG guideline such as `1.1 Text Alternatives`, and the subgroups below it are the success criteria such as `1.1.1 Non-text Content`. Each level carries the number of pages affected and the number of problems recorded, so this is the response to drive a drill-down.

Only groups that produced at least one problem appear, and within them only the subgroups that did, all sorted by name. An empty `groups` array therefore means the run found nothing, not that it has not finished. The `id` fields are the ids to pass as `group` and `subgroup` to `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}`. A run of another project, or an id that is not a run, answers `500` rather than `404`.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project the run belongs to. A project this account cannot read answers `404` before the handler runs.

parameters.name: reportId
parameters.description: ID of the accessibility run — the `id` from `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}`, or the `id` that `POST /v1/accessibility/{projectId}` returned. It is not checked here, so an id that is not a run of this project answers `500` from the handler rather than `404`.

200.description: The run’s guideline groups and subgroups, with page and problem counts.

id.description: ID of the guideline group. Pass it as `group` to `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}` to see only the pages with problems in it.

name.description: Name of the guideline group as the checker stores it, for example `1.1 Text Alternatives`. An empty string when no translation exists for it.

pages.description: Number of pages in the run with at least one problem in this group or in any of the subgroups listed under it.

problems.description: Number of problem instances recorded for this group across all pages, including those filed under its subgroups.

id.description: ID of the subgroup. Pass it as `subgroup` to `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}` to see only the pages with problems in it.

name.description: Name of the subgroup — the success criterion below the guideline, for example `1.1.1 Non-text Content`. An empty string when no translation exists for it.

pages.description: Number of pages in the run with at least one problem in this subgroup.

problems.description: Number of problem instances recorded for this subgroup across all pages.

subgroups.description: Subgroups of this group that produced a problem, sorted by name. Empty when all of its problems are filed directly under the group.

groups.description: Guideline groups that produced a problem, sorted by name. Empty when the run found nothing.

get.description:
Returns everything the checker found on one page of a run, split into four buckets and nested group, then subgroup, then finding. `knownProblems` are confirmed violations, `likelyProblems` are findings the checker believes but cannot prove without a person looking, `potentialProblems` are findings that may be violations, and `archived` holds findings that have been archived for this page — every finding also states its own `type` and `isArchived`.

`itemId` in the path is the `id` of the page row from `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}`, not that row’s `itemId` field, which is the page’s own id. Groups are WCAG guidelines and subgroups are the success criteria below them; a page with nothing in a bucket returns an empty array for it. A page or run that does not belong to this project answers `500` rather than `404`, and so does a path id that is not a number.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project the run belongs to. A project this account cannot read answers `404` before the handler runs.

parameters.name: reportId
parameters.description: ID of the accessibility run — the `id` from `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}`, or the `id` that `POST /v1/accessibility/{projectId}` returned. It is not checked here, so an id that is not a run of this project answers `500` from the handler rather than `404`.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: ID of the page row — the `id` field of `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/{reportId}`, not that row’s `itemId` field. It is not checked here, so a row that is not part of this run answers `500`.

200.description: The findings for one page of a run, split by severity.

name.description: Name of the guideline group or, one level down, of the subgroup the findings belong to. `null` for findings the checker could not attribute to that level.
Name of the subgroup — the WCAG success criterion under the guideline, for example `1.1.1 Non-text Content`. `null` for findings filed under the group but not under a named subgroup.

id.description: ID of this finding, unique within the page’s results.

type.description: Severity the finding was recorded at: `knownProblems` is a confirmed violation, `likelyProblems` one the checker believes but cannot prove automatically, `potentialProblems` one that may be a violation. Inside `archived` it says what the finding was before it was archived.

error.description: What the check found, in the checker’s words — the message to show a reader. `null` when none was recorded.

sourceCode.description: Fragment of the page’s HTML the finding points at, when the checker captured one. `null` when it did not.

repair.description: Suggested repair for the finding, written by the checker. `null` when it offers none.

isArchived.description: Whether this finding has been archived, which is `true` for everything under `archived` and `false` in the three live buckets.

problems.description: Findings recorded for this subgroup on this page. Empty when the subgroup only appears for its archived findings.

subgroups.description: Subgroups with findings in this bucket, sorted by name. Empty when the bucket holds no findings for the page.

knownProblems.description: Confirmed violations on this page, grouped by WCAG guideline and then by success criterion.

get.description:
Lists the PDF files the checker has found on, or been given for, a project — one row per file with the file’s check state and its problem counts. `id` is the id `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/pdf/{itemId}` takes for the per-criterion results. Checking is asynchronous: a file sits at `queued` and moves through `running` to `completed`, and its counts fill in as it goes.

Files that were deleted are excluded from the list, so `deleted` never appears in `state` here even though the field can hold it. `limit` defaults to 50 and is lowered to 100 if you ask for more; `page` is 1-based. Without `orderBy` the most recently modified file comes first, and `orderDir` defaults to `asc` when you pass an `orderBy` without a direction.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Substring matched against the file’s URL or its filename, so a search for `invoice` finds both a URL ending in `invoice.pdf` and a file named that way.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Restrict to files found on the project’s own domain (`internal`) or to files linked from another domain (`external`). Omit to include both kinds, and uploaded files with them.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Field to order by: `date` orders by when the file was last modified and then when it was created, the other three by that problem count. Omit it to get the most recently modified files first.

parameters.name: orderDir
parameters.description: Direction applied to `orderBy`, defaulting to `asc` — pass `desc` to rank the largest counts first. Without an `orderBy` the ordering is newest-modified first whatever this is set to.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number to return. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of files to return. Defaults to 50; values above 100 are lowered to 100 rather than rejected.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project whose PDF files are being read. A project this account cannot read answers `404` before the handler runs.

200.description: A page of the project’s PDF files, with their check state and counts.

total.description: Number of files matching the filters, ignoring paging — `ceil(total / limit)` pages are available.

limit.description: Page size that was applied: the `limit` you sent capped at 100, or 50 when you sent none.

pageSize.description: Number of pages at this `limit`, `ceil(total / limit)`, not the number of rows in this response.

id.description: ID of the PDF item. It is the `itemId` of `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/pdf/{itemId}`, which reports the file’s per-criterion results.

url.description: URL the PDF was found at, or the address of the uploaded file. An empty string when none was recorded.

filename.description: Name of the PDF file as stored, for example `report-2024.pdf`. An empty string when none was recorded.

isExternal.description: Whether the file lives on another domain than the project’s, which is what the `external` `location` filter selects. `false` for files on the project’s own domain and for uploads.

isUploaded.description: Whether the file was uploaded to the account rather than discovered by crawling. Uploads have no crawled URL of their own.

state.description: Check lifecycle of the file: `completed` when the checker has results for it, `running` while it is being checked, `queued` while it waits to be checked, `deleted` for a removed file, and `unknown` for a stored value the API does not recognize. `deleted` is declared for completeness but this list filters deleted files out, so it is never returned here.

status.description: Status text the checker stores beside `state`, passed through as recorded. Prose rather than a fixed set, so read `state` for the lifecycle. `null` when none was recorded.

error.description: Message the check ended with when it failed. `null` when the file has not failed, including while it is still queued or running.

errorReason.description: The checker’s own reason for `error`, in its words rather than a fixed vocabulary. `null` when it recorded none.

knownProblems.description: Known problems in the file: findings the checker is certain are violations. `0` when it found none or has not finished.

likelyProblems.description: Likely problems in the file: findings the checker believes are violations but cannot confirm without a person looking. `0` when there are none.

potentialProblems.description: Potential problems in the file: findings that may be violations. `0` when there are none.

archivedKnownProblems.description: Known problems in the file that have since been archived, so they are kept for history but no longer counted in `knownProblems`. `0` when nothing is archived.

archivedLikelyProblems.description: Likely problems in the file that have since been archived and are no longer counted in `likelyProblems`. `0` when nothing is archived.

archivedPotentialProblems.description: Potential problems in the file that have since been archived and are no longer counted in `potentialProblems`. `0` when nothing is archived.

created.description: ISO 8601 date and time the file was added to the project.

items.description: The page of files. Empty when no file of the project matches the filters.

get.description:
Returns every criterion the checker evaluated for one PDF as a flat list, one row per criterion, so a client can render the file’s full checklist instead of the counts that `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/pdf` summarizes. `itemId` is the `id` of a file row from that list.

Each row names its family in `guideline` and its criterion in `criteria`; match those against `GET /v1/accessibility/pdf-guidelines` for the criterion’s title, explanation and link. `valid` is what the checker decided, `needsManualCheck` marks criteria a person still has to confirm, and archived results are included with `isArchived: true` rather than dropped. A file that does not belong to this project answers `500` rather than `404`, and so does a path id that is not a number.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project whose PDF files are being read. A project this account cannot read answers `404` before the handler runs.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: ID of the PDF file — the `id` field of `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}/pdf`. It is not checked here, so a file that is not part of this project answers `500` rather than `404`.

200.description: The per-criterion results for one PDF file.

id.description: ID of this check result row.

guideline.description: Guideline family the criterion belongs to, matching a key of `GET /v1/accessibility/pdf-guidelines` — `WCAG20` for the WCAG 2.0 checklist.

criteria.description: Number of the success criterion this result is for, for example `1.1.1`. Match it against `criteria` in `GET /v1/accessibility/pdf-guidelines` for the title and link.

valid.description: Whether the file passed this criterion, as the checker recorded it. `false` covers both a failed check and a criterion nobody has confirmed yet, so read `needsManualCheck` before treating it as a failure.

group.description: Severity bucket the checker put this result in: `known_problems` is a confirmed failure, `likely_problems` a probable one, `potential_problems` a possible one, and `unknown` a confidence the API does not map. Note the snake_case names — they match the `orderBy` values of the file list, not the camelCase buckets of the web report.

needsManualCheck.description: Whether a person has to verify this criterion for the file, because the automated check cannot decide it.

message.description: Message the checker recorded for this result. It is `null` in every response today: the text is returned under a `messages` key that this response schema does not declare, so it is dropped when the response is serialized.

isArchived.description: Whether this result has been archived for the file. Archived results are still returned here, so a client that wants only live findings has to filter on this.

result.description: One row per criterion the checker evaluated for the file, ordered by criterion number. Empty when it has not evaluated the file yet.

get.description:
Lists the sitemap items of a project that carry at least one published comment, most recently commented first. One row describes one sitemap item — a page, or a container that groups items — not one comment, and an item nobody has commented on is never listed, so an empty `items` array means no commented item matched `search` or that `page` is past the last one.

An item that has been deleted from the sitemap is not listed even if comments remain on it, and `lastActivity` is taken from published comments only — so the date shown is the date of a comment a reader can still see. This is stricter than the application’s own comments roll-up, which counts a deleted comment as activity.

`id` is the sitemap item id, the identifier `GET /v1/project/{projectId}/item` reports and the one `GET /v1/comments/{projectId}/{itemId}` expects. `comments` is how many published comments the item has and `lastActivity` is when the newest of them was written, which is the order the list arrives in unless you ask for `orderBy=comments`.

Paging is `page` (1-based, default 1) and `limit` (default 20, silently capped at 100). `total` counts every commented item that matches `search`, not just this page, and `pageSize` is how many pages that total makes. Nothing is queued: the endpoint reads stored comments and answers immediately.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items one page holds. Defaults to 20 when omitted. Must be a positive whole number; a value above 100 is lowered to 100 rather than refused.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based number of the page to return. Defaults to 1, the first page. Must be a positive whole number.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Return only items whose title contains this text. A plain substring test on the title — not a prefix or word search — with surrounding whitespace trimmed. An empty value applies no filter.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Order of the list: `lastActivity` puts the item whose newest comment is the most recent first, `comments` puts the item with the most published comments first. Defaults to `lastActivity` when omitted.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project, the numeric id every project endpoint takes. A value that is not a positive whole number answers 400 before the handler runs.

200.description: A page of the project’s sitemap items that have comments.

total.description: Number of sitemap items in the project that have at least one published comment and match `search`. Independent of `page` and `limit`.

limit.description: Items per page this response was built with: the `limit` that was sent, or 20 when none was, after the 100 cap was applied.

page.description: 1-based number of the page this response holds: the `page` that was sent, or 1 when none was.

pageSize.description: Number of pages `total` divides into at this `limit`, rounded up. It is a page count rather than an item count, despite the name: 41 commented items at `limit` 20 report `pageSize` 3.

id.description: ID of the sitemap item, as `GET /v1/project/{projectId}/item` reports it and as `GET /v1/comments/{projectId}/{itemId}` expects it in the path.

title.description: Title of the item as it appears in the project’s sitemap.

type.description: Kind of sitemap item: `link` for an item that stands for a page of the site, `container` for a grouping item — the kind the project’s `buckets` count reports. Comments can be attached to either kind, so both appear in this list.

url.description: URL the item stands for. Null, or absent, when the item has no URL of its own — a container may have none.

comments.description: Number of published comments on the item. At least 1: items with none are not listed.

lastActivity.description: ISO 8601 date and time, in UTC, when the newest published comment on the item was written. This is what the default order sorts on. `null` is possible in one case: the stored comment count on the item says comments exist while no published comment can be read — a counter left behind by a writer that never refreshed it. Writing a comment through the API recounts it and repairs the row.

items.description: One entry per commented sitemap item: exactly the rows of this page.

get.summary: List every comment in a project
get.description:
The project’s whole conversation, newest first: every published comment on every published item, each row naming the item it belongs to so a client can link back or call the per-item read. It is the moderation view rather than the reading view — `GET /v1/comments/{projectId}/{itemId}` answers one item oldest first, while this answers the whole project newest first.

`search` matches the comment text, not the item title; pass `itemId` to narrow the feed to one item, which makes it usable as a queue for a single page. Comments on deleted items and comments that were deleted themselves are left out, so a row here is always a comment a reader could still be shown.

Paging is `page` (1-based, default 1) and `limit` (default 20, capped at 100). `total` counts every comment that matches `search` and `itemId`, not just this page.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based number of the page to return. Defaults to 1, the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many comments one page holds. Defaults to 20 when omitted; a value above 100 is lowered to 100 rather than refused.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Direction to sort in: `desc` for newest first, the default, `asc` for oldest first. Ties within a second are broken by comment id, so pages do not overlap.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Return only comments whose text contains this text. A plain substring test with surrounding whitespace trimmed; the item title is not searched. An empty value applies no filter.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: Return only comments on this sitemap item. An id that is not in this project matches nothing rather than failing.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project, the numeric id every project endpoint takes. A value that is not a positive whole number answers 400 before the handler runs.

200.description: A page of every comment in the project.

total.description: Number of published comments in the project that match `search` and `itemId`. Independent of `page` and `limit`.

limit.description: Comments per page this response was built with: the `limit` that was sent, or 20 when none was, after the 100 cap was applied.

page.description: 1-based number of the page this response holds: the `page` that was sent, or 1 when none was.

pageSize.description: Number of pages `total` divides into at this `limit`, rounded up. It is a page count rather than an item count.

id.description: ID of the comment itself — not the sitemap item id, which is `itemId` here and the last path segment of the per-item routes.

comment.description: Text of the comment exactly as it was stored, passed through untouched: the API neither renders nor formats it. Surrounding whitespace was trimmed when it was written; the value is between 1 and 1000 characters.

name.description: Name the commenter’s account carries, taken from their display name when the comment was written. An empty string when the account has none, never `null`.

email.description: Email address the commenter’s account carries. An empty string when none is stored, never `null`. This is personal data, and it is the value `picture` is computed from.

picture.description: Avatar URL on gravatar.com, built from the MD5 hash of the commenter’s lowercased, trimmed email address. An empty string when there is no email to hash, never `null`. The image is served by gravatar.com, not by this API.

created.description: ISO 8601 date and time, in UTC, when the comment was written. What `order` sorts on.

modified.description: ISO 8601 date and time, in UTC, when the comment was last edited, or `null` when it has never been edited since it was written. A deletion also stamps the row, but a deleted comment is never returned, so a value here always means an edit.

itemId.description: ID of the sitemap item the comment is attached to, as `GET /v1/project/{projectId}/item` reports it and as the per-item routes take in their last path segment.

itemTitle.description: Title of the sitemap item the comment is attached to, as the project’s tree shows it. An empty string when the item has no title.

itemUrl.description: URL of the sitemap item the comment is attached to, or `null` when it has none — a container usually does not.

items.description: The comments on this page, newest first unless `order=asc` was sent, each carrying the item it belongs to.

get.summary: List the comments on a sitemap item
get.description:
Returns the comments on one sitemap item, oldest first — the order a conversation reads in — unless `order=desc` asks for the newest first. Only published comments are returned, and only on a published item of a published project; a comment that was deleted stops appearing here while the row stays in the database.

`itemId` is a sitemap item id, produced by `GET /v1/project/{projectId}/item`, and `projectId` is the project that item belongs to. An item that has been deleted, or that belongs to another project, answers `404 item_not_found` rather than an empty list — the API no longer hides the difference between “no comments” and “no such item”. An item that exists and has no comments answers an empty `items` array.

Paging is `page` (1-based, default 1) and `limit` (default 20, capped at 100), and `total` counts every comment that matches `search`, not just this page. `search` is a substring test on the comment text.
