post.summary: Post a comment on a sitemap item
post.description:
Adds a comment to a sitemap item and publishes it immediately — the application has no approval step, so a comment posted here is visible to every reader of the project at once. The commenter is the authenticated user: `name` and `email` come from their account, and a client cannot post on somebody else’s behalf.

The item must belong to this project and still be published, and the project must be published itself. Both are checked before anything is written, so an id from another account’s project cannot be commented on through the call — the application’s own public comment path does not make that check.

One transaction writes the comment, the row that files it under the project, and the item’s comment counts, which is the same set of rows the application writes. No email is sent: the application’s mailer is the only thing that sends comment notifications. The response is the stored comment in the shape the reads use, `201`, with its `itemId` so a client can build a link without keeping the path.

A person may post as many comments on one item as they like, on a page or on a container, exactly as the application allows.

delete.description:
Deletes a comment the way the application does: a **soft** delete. The row keeps its text and the row that files it under the project; only its state changes, which is what every read filters on, so the comment stops appearing everywhere without anything being lost.

The item’s published-comment count is recomputed in the same transaction, so `GET /v1/comments/{projectId}` and the item read agree immediately. No email is sent and nothing else is touched — the application does not notify anybody about a deletion either.

The call is idempotent: deleting a comment that is already deleted answers `204` again rather than `404`, because the caller asked for a state the comment is already in. An id from another project, or an item that no longer exists, still answers `404`. There is no restore — a deleted comment can only be brought back in the application’s database.

get.description:
Returns one page of content assignments: the work items an account creates against a project, or against a single page of one. One row is one assignment — what it covers (`projectId`, plus `itemId` when it is about one page), when it starts and is due, whether it is still open, and the page’s title and URL beside the assignment’s own title.

The list spans every project in the account that still holds assignments. A caller who may see account-wide assignments gets every assignment in the account and can narrow the list with `filterByUserId`; everyone else sees only the assignments assigned to them. Paging is `page` and `limit` (defaults 1 and 20, maximum 100), and `total` counts every match before the page is cut, so keep requesting pages until you have collected `total` rows. Filters combine with AND: `search` matches the assignment title only, while `category`, `workflow` and `tags` match the page the assignment is attached to, so an assignment covering a whole project never matches them.

A row carries no assigned users and no metadata. To see those, fetch one assignment with `GET /v1/assignments/assignment/{id}`. For counts alone use `GET /v1/assignments/totals`, or `GET /v1/assignments/{projectId}/totals` when you already know the project.

get.description:
Counts assignments instead of returning them: how many there are in all, how many are open, how many are completed, how many were created in the last seven days and how many are past due. Nothing about an individual assignment comes back, so this is the cheap call behind a badge or a dashboard tile; use `GET /v1/assignments` when you need the rows.

The figures follow the caller’s reach rather than a project you name. When the account holds assignments in more than one project the counts cover the whole account — projects in the published or pending state, and only assignments whose page still exists — and `filterByUserId` narrows them; a caller without account-wide visibility is always narrowed to their own assignments, whatever they send. With zero or one such project the handler takes a per-project path with no project id to key on, and the request fails with a 500 instead of answering counts: for a single-project account call `GET /v1/assignments/{projectId}/totals` instead.

`recent` and `pastDue` are evaluated against the database clock on every call, so they change over time even when no assignment is edited.

recent.description: Of `total`, the assignments created in the last seven days. The window is rolling and measured against the database clock at the moment of the call, not a calendar week, so the number falls as assignments age past seven days without anything else changing.

pastDue.description: Of `total`, the open assignments whose due date falls before today by the database clock. Completed assignments are never counted here, however late they were finished.

The same five counts as `GET /v1/assignments/totals`, restricted to the assignments of one project: `total`, `open`, `completed`, `recent` (created in the last seven days) and `pastDue` (open and overdue). The numbers are derived from the project’s assignments alone — every one of them, including any whose page no longer exists — so this is also the call to make when the account-wide endpoint answers a 500.

The project must be readable by the token: an id that is not in the account answers 404 `project_not_found` and one the caller may not read answers 403 `unauthorized_access`, both before the handler runs. A project with no assignments answers zeros rather than an error, and a `projectId` that is not a number fails the lookup with a 500 rather than a 400.

`filterByUserId` narrows the counts to the assignments of the users listed, but only for a caller who may see other people’s assignments; for everyone else the parameter is ignored and their own assignments are counted. Use `GET /v1/assignments/{projectId}` to list the assignments behind the numbers.

parameters.name: filterByUserId
parameters.description: Comma-separated user ids to count assignments for, for example `12,34`; an assignment counts once when at least one of those users is assigned to it. Only a caller who may see other people’s assignments can narrow by somebody else — for everyone else the value is ignored and their own assignments are counted.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: ID of the project whose assignments to count, as returned by `GET /v1/project`.

200.description: Counts of the project’s assignments.

total.description: Assignments in scope, counting both open and completed ones. Assignments in any other stored state are excluded from every count in this object.

open.description: Of `total`, the assignments still to be done (state 1).

recent.description: Of `total`, the assignments created in the last seven days. The window is rolling and measured against the database clock at the moment of the call, not a calendar week, so the number falls as assignments age past seven days without anything else changing.

pastDue.description: Of `total`, the open assignments whose due date falls before today by the database clock. Completed assignments are never counted here, however late they were finished.

get.description:
Returns one assignment in full: the same fields as a row of `GET /v1/assignments`, plus `users` — the people it is assigned to, with the display name and preferred color stored for each — and `metadata`, the free-form object stored with it. Use it when you already hold an assignment id and need the fields the list endpoints leave out.

Unlike the lists this operation returns the assignment whatever its state. It answers 404 when no assignment carries that id, and 403 when the assignment’s project is not one of the account’s published projects that hold an open or completed assignment — so a 403 does not always mean the assignment belongs to somebody else: an assignment in a project that is still pending, or one whose own state is neither open nor completed, lands there too.

Both of those failures carry a `message` and nothing else: there is no `error` or `code` key to branch on, so read the message. Project-wide failures elsewhere in the API do include those keys, which is why the schemas below document every member as optional.

To resolve what the assignment refers to, read the project with `GET /v1/project/{projectId}` and the page with `GET /v1/inventory/{projectId}/{itemId}`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the assignment, as returned in the `id` of a row from `GET /v1/assignments` or `GET /v1/assignments/{projectId}`. Only the numeric id is accepted, never the title or a page id.

200.description: The assignment, with its assigned users and metadata.

id.description: ID of the assignment.

projectId.description: ID of the project the assignment belongs to. Read the project with `GET /v1/project/{projectId}`.

itemId.description: ID of the inventory page the assignment is attached to, usable with `GET /v1/inventory/{projectId}/{itemId}`. `null` for an assignment that covers the project as a whole instead of one page: the stored value is `0` and this API reports that as `null`.

title.description: Title of the assignment itself, as whoever created it wrote it. Not the page title. `null` when the assignment has no title.

note.description: Free-form note stored on the assignment. `null` when it has none. The stored note format is not returned, so treat the text as unformatted.

type.description: Assignment type as stored on the record. Neither the schema nor the handler constrains or enumerates it, so treat it as free-form text. `null` when unset.

status.description: `open` while the assignment is still to be done (stored state 1) and `completed` for every other stored state. Unlike the list endpoints this operation returns the assignment whatever its state, so a state the lists never show is reported here as `completed`.

startDate.description: Start of the window the assignment is planned for, as an ISO 8601 date and time in UTC with a trailing `Z`.

dueDate.description: Deadline of the assignment, as an ISO 8601 date and time in UTC with a trailing `Z`. An open assignment whose due date has passed is what the totals endpoints count as past due.

created.description: When the assignment was created, as an ISO 8601 date and time in UTC with a trailing `Z`.

finished.description: When the assignment was completed, as an ISO 8601 date and time in UTC with a trailing `Z`. `null` until it has been completed.

metadata.description: Free-form object stored with the assignment — an untyped map of string keys to any JSON value. The API does not validate its keys or values and returns whatever was stored, so read it defensively rather than assuming a shape. `{}` when the assignment carries no metadata.

id.description: ID of the assigned user, the same id other endpoints accept as `filterByUserId`.

name.description: Display name of the assigned user, as stored on their user record.

color.description: Color recorded in the assigned user’s preferences, as the application stores it. Free-form, so treat it as an opaque value rather than a fixed palette.

users.description: Users the assignment is assigned to. Empty when nobody is assigned; the list endpoints do not return this array at all.

post.summary: Upload a file and get a key to import it
post.description:
Uploads one file and returns a key that an import endpoint accepts in place of the file itself. Use it when the file is large, lives somewhere your integration cannot stream from, or is imported more than once: send it here, then pass the returned `key` as `fileKey` to the import that consumes it.

The request is `multipart/form-data` carrying a `purpose` field and a single `file` part. `purpose` is a contract rather than a label: it fixes the media types the file may have, the 64 MB limit, and the only endpoint allowed to spend the key — `POST /v1/project/text` for `project_text`, `POST /v1/project/xml` for `project_xml`. The declared type is checked on the way in and again when the key is used, so one purpose cannot spend a key issued for the other.

Keys are account-scoped and not consumed. The upload itself stays in staging, and each import that resolves the key copies the bytes into the data bucket and serves the project from there; a key that belongs to another account is refused when it is used, with the same answer as a key that never existed.

purpose.description: What the file will be imported as. It decides the media types and the size limit the file must satisfy, and the one endpoint that can spend the returned key. `project_text` accepts any `text/*` file, plus `application/json`, `application/xml` and `application/yaml`, up to 64 MB, and its key is used by `POST /v1/project/text`. `project_xml` accepts `text/plain`, `text/xml` and `application/xml`, up to 64 MB, and its key is used by `POST /v1/project/xml`.
purpose.title: Purpose

file.description: The file to store, sent as the request’s one file part. Its declared media type must be one `purpose` accepts, and it may not be empty or larger than 64 MB.

201.description: The stored file and the key that the import endpoint for its purpose accepts in its place.

key.description: Identifier of the stored file. Send it as `fileKey` to the import endpoint that matches its purpose — `POST /v1/project/text` for `project_text`, `POST /v1/project/xml` for `project_xml` — instead of sending the file again. It is bound to the uploading account and is not consumed by use, so one upload can back several imports.

name.description: Original filename, as the client sent it, with any directory removed. The import endpoint that spends the key uses it as the new project’s title.

size.description: Length of the stored file in bytes, counted from the bytes received rather than taken from a request header.

mimeType.description: Media type the client declared for the file, lower-cased and with parameters such as `; charset=utf-8` removed. This is the value the purpose’s allowlist was checked against; the bytes themselves are not sniffed.

400.description: The upload was rejected. `file_required` when the request carries no `file` part, `invalid_file_type` when the declared media type is not accepted for that `purpose`, and `file_empty` when the file has no bytes. A missing or unrecognised `purpose` is caught by request validation instead, and its `message` names the field.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: The user the access token belongs to. `GET /v1/user/me` is the cheapest way to check that a token works.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description:
Projects, and the crawls and imports that create them.

**Typical sequence:** `POST /v1/project/url` to crawl a website, poll `GET /v1/project/url/{id}` until the crawl finishes, then read the project with `GET /v1/project/{projectId}`. A text or XML import follows the same shape with its own create and poll pair. The full recipes are in the Workflows section of the guide.

tags.name: Sitemap
tags.description:
Edit a project’s sitemap tree: add, change, move, duplicate, sort and delete items, assign categories, workflow statuses, tags and colors in bulk, and walk the project’s undo history.

**Typical sequence:** read the tree with `GET /v1/project/{projectId}/item`, change it with the writes below, and reverse a mistake with `POST /v1/project/{projectId}/item/history/undo`. The history is the same one the application’s editor uses, so a step recorded here appears in its Undo list and the other way round.

These are the only write endpoints in this API that answer 409 for a project that is not published: a pending crawl or an archived project can still be read, but not edited.

tags.name: Inventory
tags.description: The links a crawl found, page by page. `GET /v1/inventory/{projectId}` pages through every link and `/summary` answers the counts. Reads a finished crawl, so crawl a project first.

tags.name: Audit
tags.description:
The content audit of a project: duplicated and orphaned content, titles and descriptions, crawlable and indexable pages.

There is no endpoint here that starts an audit — the application runs it. `GET /v1/audit/{projectId}` is the history of runs; every other endpoint reads the latest one.

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: Google Analytics 4 data for a property linked to the project. `startDate` and `endDate` are required on every endpoint, and the numbers are read from stored data rather than queried from Google.

tags.name: Visibility
tags.description:
Keyword positions over time.

**Typical sequence:** add keywords with `POST /v1/visibility/{projectId}/keyword`, group and label them with the `PATCH` endpoints, then read their positions with `GET /v1/visibility/{projectId}`. `GET /v1/visibility/locales` lists the `locale` values that are accepted.

tags.name: Accessibility
tags.description:
Accessibility runs against a project, and the reports they produce.

**Typical sequence:** start a run with `POST /v1/accessibility/{projectId}`, list the runs with `GET /v1/accessibility/{projectId}` to get a `reportId`, then read that report. Every endpoint below the run takes that `reportId`.

tags.name: Comments
tags.description:
Comments left on a project and on the sitemap items inside it. `GET /v1/comments/{projectId}` lists only the items that have comments, `GET /v1/comments/{projectId}/all` reads them across the project, and `GET /v1/comments/{projectId}/{itemId}` reads one item’s thread.

**Typical sequence:** find a page with `GET /v1/comments/{projectId}`, read it with `GET /v1/comments/{projectId}/{itemId}`, then write with `POST` and correct with `PATCH` or `DELETE`. A comment is published the moment it is posted — there is no approval step — and a delete is a soft delete that can be repeated safely but cannot be undone through the API.

tags.name: Assignments
tags.description: Work assigned to users. `GET /v1/assignments` spans every project in the account; `GET /v1/assignments/{projectId}` narrows to one, and the `totals` pair answers the counts behind them.

tags.name: Files
tags.description: Upload a file once, then pass the `key` it returns as `fileKey` to an endpoint that accepts a file instead of sending it again. The import endpoints that accept a key are listed by the `purpose` you upload with.
